headline: A paper finds local serving protocols can distort tool-use fidelity scores
summary: A September 2026 preprint reports that local serving behavior can be mistaken for model tool-use behavior. In the authors’ Ollama setup, static template flags reject some native tool-call requests before inference; their harness records retry exhaustion as a generic assistant turn, which can make an unrun model appear to have zero tool-call fidelity. Across four serving stacks, request handling differs. Prompt hints improve some accepted models, while forcing a uniform text protocol reduces fidelity for a model with native tool-call support. Turn-pooled and per-seed estimates differ by up to about 55 points when a looping episode dominates a thin sample. These are author-reported results from a small study, not a prevalence estimate or general model comparison.
